title: DoesItOmarchy diagnostic report, v1
description: One test run of Omarchy on one Intel Mac configuration. Submit it to POST /api/v1/reports with a source key. See https://doesitomarchy.com/api.

config.description: A configuration ID (see GET /api/v1/macs/{identifier}). Optional when identifier or hardware identify the Mac; the server then finds the configuration.

identifier.description: The model identifier (DMI product_name on Linux, hw.model on macOS).

id.description: Taken from your key; if given, it must match.

contact.description: Optional; stored only as a one-way hash, for maintainers.

tested_at.description: When the test ran, RFC 3339 with a time zone. Stored and shown in UTC.

version.description: /etc/os-release's VERSION_ID, from any channel: a release, a pre-release (rc, beta) or an edge build.

channel.description: Only needed for dev (Omarchy run from a git checkout), whose version reads like an edge build. The others follow from the version.

revision.description: A dev build's commit: omarchy-version prints "dev (<hash>)".

hardware.description: The hardware probe. Standard keys (product_name, board_id, cpu, pci, usb) identify the configuration; other keys are kept. Personal data (serials, MAC/IP addresses, host and user names) is removed before storage; please don't send it.

cpu.description: The CPU name (model name in /proc/cpuinfo, or machdep.cpu.brand_string). Tells apart configurations that share every device.

items.description: Capability ID (see GET /api/v1/capabilities) → result. Leave out what you didn't test. For a port criterion, add the connector from the configuration's layout (GET /api/v1/configs/{id}, connectors): "ports.usb-a@left-2". Each connector is then a result of its own.

evidence.description: Why it failed or only partly works: the check's output.

extras.description: Checks that aren't (yet) DoesItOmarchy criteria; shown as reported, never counted.

consent_notice.description: The notice your tool showed the tester before submitting (see /api).
